name: text-along-path
title: Text Along Path
description: A line of repeated text travels endlessly along a rounded rectangle outline, wrapping from one side to the next. It can loop on a timer or follow the reader's scroll, with room in the middle for a form.
use: A launch or waitlist page wants its call to action framed by moving text that pulls the eye.
avoid: The loop runs forever with no pause and ignores reduced motion, and words clip where the path meets the crop.
a11y: The moving words are decorative and unlabelled, and the loop never pauses for reduced-motion users. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Lowercase blue monospace words repeat in a continuous loop around a large rounded rectangle on black, running upside down and right to left along the bottom edge. In the middle sit a thin outlined email field and a solid blue Subscribe button.
behaves: The words slide clockwise around the track without a visible seam, since a second copy chases the first. Typing an address and submitting swaps the button label for a spinner, then a Done tick, and later returns to its resting state.
customise: Path data, the text, viewBox, font classes and animation mode are props, with duration, repeat count and easing for the loop and offsets for scroll mode.
weight: light: Two duplicated text paths on an SVG timer; cheap, but it animates for as long as it is visible.
demo: Repeated "join the waitlist ✉" text around an email field and a Subscribe button that ends on Done.
issues: Words are clipped mid-letter where the path runs past the crop edges.
On the bottom run the text is upside down, so it reads right to left and is hard to parse.
polishWhy: Crisp seamless loop and a strong accent; clipping and the inverted bottom run let it down.
